note: Authored Study Room quiz items. Code items are validated by execution.

items.code:
int a = 7, b = 2;
System.out.println(a / b + " " + (double) a / b);
items.explanation: int / int truncates to 3. Casting a to double first makes the division floating point, 3.5.

items.code:
int big = Integer.MAX_VALUE;
System.out.println(big + 1 == Integer.MIN_VALUE);
items.explanation: Java int arithmetic wraps on overflow, so MAX_VALUE + 1 is MIN_VALUE.

items.prompt: average(int total, int count) must return the exact average as a double. 7 and 2 should give 3.5. Fix it.
items.explanation: Integer division happens before the result is widened; cast an operand to double first.
== compares references; new String creates a separate object. equals compares contents.
&& short-circuits: the length check is false, so xs[0] is never read.

items.prompt: isTeen(int age) must return true for 13 through 19 inclusive. Fix the boundaries.
items.explanation: Inclusive boundaries need >= and <=.
i takes 0, 2 and 4, so the body runs three times.

items.prompt: sumTo(int n) should return 1 + 2 + ... + n. It misses n. Fix it.
items.explanation: Use <= so the loop includes n.
Java passes a copy of the primitive value, so the caller's v is unchanged.
Overload resolution picks the exact type: 5 is an int literal and 5L is a long.

items.prompt: distance(int a, int b) must return a non-negative distance. It can return negative numbers. Fix it.
items.explanation: Math.abs makes the result independent of argument order.
char + int promotes to int (98). Casting back to char gives 'b'.
Strings are immutable; toUpperCase returns a new String that was discarded.

items.prompt: countMatches(String[] words, String target) must count words that are exactly equal to target. It also counts words that merely contain it. Fix it.
items.explanation: contains matches substrings; equals compares the whole string's contents (never ==, which compares references).
b refers to the same array object as a; use a.clone() or Arrays.copyOf for a copy.
New int arrays are filled with 0.

items.prompt: maxOf(int[] values) returns the largest value of a non-empty array. It throws ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException. Fix it.
items.explanation: The last valid index is length - 1, so the loop needs <.
getOrDefault supplies 0 for the first read; get on a missing key returns null.
merge adds 1 for each occurrence; TreeMap keeps keys sorted.

items.prompt: countOf(String[] words, String target) builds a frequency map, then returns target's count. It throws NullPointerException. Fix it.
items.explanation: get returns null for a new key and unboxing null throws; use getOrDefault.
add returns false when the element was already present; the set keeps one copy.

items.code:
Integer a = 1000, b = 1000;
System.out.println((a == b) + " " + a.equals(b));
items.explanation: Boxed values outside the -128..127 cache are separate objects, so == is false while equals is true.

items.prompt: hasDuplicate(int[] values) should return true when any value repeats. It always returns false. Fix it.
items.explanation: Check membership before adding (or use the boolean that add returns).
A static field is shared by every instance; mine belongs to each object.
Records generate equals and hashCode from their components, so equal points are found in a HashSet.

items.prompt: finalBalance(int initial, int[] changes) applies changes to an account object. A local variable in the initializer shadows the field, so the balance always starts at 0. Fix it.
items.explanation: int balance = initial declares a new local that hides the field. Assign the field itself.
parseInt throws for '12a'; the catch prints bad and finally always runs.

items.code:
Optional<String> name = Optional.empty();
System.out.println(name.orElse("guest") + " " + name.isPresent());
items.explanation: orElse supplies the fallback for an empty Optional.

items.prompt: safeAt(int[] values, int index, int fallback) must return fallback for any invalid index, including negative ones. Fix it.
items.explanation: Valid indices are 0 through length - 1; check both ends.
f sums the digits: 2 + 7 + 4 = 13.
steps(0) = steps(1) = 1, then 2, 3, 5.

items.prompt: factorial(int n) should return n! for n from 0 to 12. It recurses forever on 0. Fix it.
items.explanation: The base case must also stop at 0.

items.prompt: What is the time complexity of the loop?
items.explanation: ArrayList.contains scans the list, O(n), and it runs n times.
PriorityQueue is a min-heap by default.

items.prompt: hasPair(int[] values, int target) must not pair an element with itself. Fix it.
items.explanation: Check before adding so the set only contains earlier elements.
